purpose: Prove the turn-taking detector recognises the monologue it exists to rule out, before it is trusted to certify absence.

preparation.note: 1920 samples at 24 kHz is one Mimi frame, so activity frames map 1:1 onto token frames.

calibration_source.origin: M0 continuation generations from the published Stage 2 and Stage 3 checkpoints
calibration_source.decoded_with: tools.decode_tokens --device cpu (the flag added in 036f5c7; 10 files in 9 s)

monologue_recognition.verdict: PASS. All 20 report user_never_active, zero speaker switches and a user speech ratio of exactly 0. The detector sees the degenerate case.

pass_criteria_for_m3.response_latency: mean within 2x the J-Moshi-ext control's, per m3/DATASET_SPEC.md
pass_criteria_for_m3.speaker_switches: must not be 0 across the 30 fixed conversations

limits: M0's user channel is digital silence, so this calibrates the FAILURE signature, not health. What a healthy conversation looks like is unknown until the J-Moshi-ext control is generated at plan step 22.

user_never_active and every other partner-channel measure is worthless as evidence that a checkpoint listens: under --model_user_stream the user stream is teacher-forced from the prompt for every arm, so it describes the prompt. It is used here only to prove the detector works.
M3 trains on strictly sequential, zero-overlap dialogues, so overlap_frames measures behaviour the model was never trained toward.
